title: Unit 1: Meeting Survival
description: Master the art of escaping syncs, parking conversations, and surviving 30,000-foot slide decks.

lessons.title: The Art of Postponement
lessons.description: Learn how to defer discussions until the end of time without looking lazy.

exercises.model: Stop talking about this in front of everyone
exercises.snark: Code for 'you are embarrassing yourself or wasting our time.'

exercises.model: Talk about this again later
exercises.snark: A promise to follow up that both parties secretly hope will be forgotten.

exercises.model: More time or energy
exercises.snark: Treating humans as Ethernet cables since 1999.

exercises.model: I have another meeting or I just want to leave
exercises.snark: A polite way to escape before someone assigns you an action item.

pairs: Stop talking about this in front of everyone
I have another meeting or I just want to leave

exercises.email: Hey team, quick sync: let’s table the architectural refactor discussion, put database sharding in the parking lot, and double-click on Q4 deliverables instead.
options: He wants to deeply optimize the database architecture tonight.
He wants to avoid technical problems and focus only on short-term sales targets.
He is taking everyone to a literal parking lot for team bonding.
He wants the engineers to build new database tables immediately.
exercises.why: 'Table' and 'parking lot' are corporate graveyard terms to shut down complex engineering work.

lessons.title: Meeting Escapes & Bio Breaks
lessons.description: Polite escape hatches, bio breaks, and fake hard stops to protect your sanity.

exercises.model: Explain or analyze this complicated mess
exercises.snark: Borrowing moving-day terminology for a slide deck with too many bullet points.

exercises.model: Meet to coordinate
exercises.snark: Because 'talk to each other' doesn't sound expensive enough on a timesheet.

exercises.model: Go to the restroom
exercises.snark: Reframing basic human biology as an enterprise-grade maintenance window.

exercises.model: Try to do an impossibly large task
exercises.snark: Good advice, but usually said by someone whose only job is attending the meeting.

pairs: Explain or analyze this complicated mess
Try to do an impossibly large task

exercises.subject: Urgent: High-Altitude Alignment
exercises.email: Team, I have a hard stop at 2:00 PM for a bio break, but net-net we need a 30,000-foot view of why the pipeline is stalled. Who has bandwidth to drive this?
options: He is volunteering to do the deep technical investigation himself.
He wants someone else to do the work while he leaves in 5 minutes.
He is inviting everyone on an airplane ride at 30,000 feet.
He is extending the meeting by two hours.
exercises.why: A 'hard stop' combined with 'who has bandwidth' means 'assign someone else before I escape.'

lessons.title: Alignment & High-Altitude Views
lessons.description: High-elevation metaphors to hide the fact that nobody has looked at the details.

exercises.model: Make noticeable progress
exercises.snark: Mechanical metaphor for slightly altering a graph during an All-Hands.

exercises.model: Easy wins requiring minimal effort
exercises.snark: If it was truly low-hanging, an intern would have already plucked it.

exercises.model: High-level overview without details
exercises.snark: The perspective from which all of your disastrous planning looks smooth.

exercises.model: The final conclusion or bottom line
exercises.snark: When regular 'net' wasn't emphatic enough to describe your net loss.

pairs: The final conclusion or bottom line

exercises.email: Let's not boil the ocean here. What is the low-hanging fruit we can pluck before the board meeting so we can show we moved the needle?
options: She wants to solve the most difficult systemic problems first.
She wants quick cosmetic fixes that look good on a slide deck.
She wants to buy fresh fruit for the board members.
She is advocating for ocean conservation.
exercises.why: 'Low-hanging fruit' means doing whatever takes 10 minutes so executives can brag to the board.

boss.title: The Friday 4:30 PM Sync Evader
boss.prompt: Decline an invite to a 4:30 PM Friday sync from your skip-level manager. You are not going. Sound enthusiastic, protect your weekend, and use corporate meeting speak. Avoid plain negative words!
boss.hint: Try using phrases like: 'hard stop', 'bandwidth', 'circle back', 'take this offline', 'touch base', or 'parking lot'.

title: Unit 2: Email Passive-Aggression
description: Decode weaponized pleasantries, lethal paper trails, and presumptive compliance.

lessons.title: The Opening Salvo
lessons.description: How to translate the razor-sharp blade of "per my last email" and friendly bumps.

exercises.model: Can you not read?
exercises.snark: The sharpest, most legally permissible dagger in corporate correspondence.

exercises.model: Pay attention to what you ignored 4 days ago
exercises.snark: Neither friendly, nor a gentle reminder. A ticking corporate countdown.

exercises.text: Bumping this to top of your inbox
exercises.model: Notice me
exercises.snark: I am actively cluttering your inbox to satisfy my anxiety.

exercises.model: Creating a paper trail so you cannot deny this
exercises.snark: Weaponized recap designed to prevent future amnesia.

pairs: Pay attention to what you ignored 4 days ago
Bumping this to top of your inbox
Creating a paper trail so you cannot deny this

exercises.subject: Re: Project Timeline Delay
exercises.email: Per my last email, the revised milestone deck was attached on Tuesday. Bumping this to the top of your inbox. Please advise on how you wish to proceed.
options: Todd is politely asking if you are having a nice week.
Todd is furious that you ignored his email and is creating a paper trail to blame you.
Todd accidentally deleted the milestone deck and needs a new copy.
Todd wants to collaborate in person over coffee.
exercises.why: 'Per my last email' + 'bumping this' is the corporate equivalent of slapping you with a glove.

lessons.title: Paper Trails & Blame Shifting
lessons.description: CC’ing the entire leadership chain to ensure mutual assured destruction.

exercises.model: Look at this so you share the blame if it fails
exercises.snark: Spreading culpability like peanut butter across the org chart.

exercises.model: You are wrong, and I brought receipts
exercises.snark: Pretending to invite feedback while delivering a lethal checkmate.

exercises.model: Summoning witnesses and backup
exercises.snark: Bringing the cavalry because this email chain has escalated to a standoff.

exercises.text: Resending in case this got buried
exercises.model: I know you saw it and chose peace
exercises.snark: Politely calling out your deliberate evasion tactics.

pairs: Look at this so you share the blame if it fails
You are wrong, and I brought receipts
Resending in case this got buried
I know you saw it and chose peace

exercises.subject: FWD: Vendor Contract Liability
exercises.email: Attaching for your visibility. I am looping in Dave from procurement, and per our offline conversation, taking myself off this thread. Thanks in advance!
options: Linda is deeply committed to managing this project personally.
Linda sees a liability disaster, dumped it on Dave, and is running away.
Linda forgot Dave’s email address.
Linda is taking the whole team out for lunch.
exercises.why: 'Taking myself off this thread' after dumping a contract means 'this bomb will not detonate near me.'

lessons.title: Presumptive Compliance
lessons.description: Saying "thanks in advance" so victims have zero legal room to say no.

exercises.model: Look at how much of your work I had to rewrite
exercises.snark: A bloody red-lined crime scene attached as a Word document.

exercises.model: I didn't care until today
exercises.snark: Standard email opener when a message has marinated for two weeks.

exercises.model: I am harassing you again
exercises.snark: The polite reminder that will never let you rest.

exercises.model: Please approve this without changes
exercises.snark: You are expected to say 'Looks great!' and nothing else.

pairs: Look at how much of your work I had to rewrite

exercises.email: Happy to discuss live! Correct me if I'm wrong, but wasn't the API contract signed off in Q1? Re-attaching with track changes for visibility.
options: Chloe is seeking feedback because she genuinely doubts her memory.
Chloe is about to destroy your argument with timestamped evidence in a live call.
Chloe wants to cancel the API contract entirely.
Chloe is praising your thoughtful code design.
exercises.why: 'Correct me if I'm wrong' accompanied by track changes is a fatal checkmate.

boss.title: The Lethal Paper Trail
boss.prompt: A coworker asked for a file that was attached to an email you sent yesterday. Write a passive-aggressive email ensuring they know they failed to read it, without directly insulting them.
boss.hint: Try using phrases like: 'per my last email', 'friendly reminder', 'attaching for your visibility', 'as discussed', or 'looping in'.

title: Unit 3: Performance Review Speak
description: Translate catastrophic feedback disguised as expansive horizons and self-starting opportunities.

lessons.title: Expanding Your Horizons
lessons.description: Why "opportunity for growth" means you failed, and how to nod serenely.

exercises.model: You are bad at this
exercises.snark: HR translation: you failed, but we must frame it as an expansive horizon.

exercises.model: Needs to do their boss's job for them
exercises.snark: Expected to babysit an executive who forgets to review slides.
ideaLabels: doing their work or babysitting them

exercises.model: Work overtime without extra pay
exercises.snark: Taking total accountability for things you have zero authority to change.

exercises.model: Dress better and speak with unearned confidence
exercises.snark: A vague, unfalsifiable critique given when they can't find real flaws.

pairs: Needs to do their boss's job for them
Dress better and speak with unearned confidence

exercises.email: In Q4, we have a real opportunity for growth. You've done well, but we need you to demonstrate more ownership, manage up, and be comfortable with ambiguity.
options: You are getting a massive raise and a promotion next week.
You will be doing your manager’s job with no instructions and no additional pay.
The company has well-defined roadmaps and clear documentation.
Your manager wants to teach you how to write code.
exercises.why: 'Comfortable with ambiguity' means management has no plan, and 'ownership' means you carry the burden.

lessons.title: Ownership & Unreasonable Demands
lessons.description: Taking ownership of things you cannot control while wearing multiple hats.

exercises.model: No one is going to train or help you
exercises.snark: Sink or swim in our undocumented legacy codebase.

exercises.model: Do we want to drink warm beer with you on Fridays?
exercises.snark: The subjective barrier that keeps corporate demographics remarkably homogeneous.

exercises.model: Posting platitudes on the internet
exercises.snark: Saying obvious things with extreme conviction and high production value.

exercises.model: The original plan failed catastrophically
exercises.snark: Scrapping six months of roadmap and calling the panic 'iterative flexibility.'

pairs: No one is going to train or help you
Do we want to drink warm beer with you on Fridays?

exercises.subject: Annual Review Follow-up
exercises.email: We value self-starters who wear multiple hats and lean in. To raise the bar on executive presence, let’s see you do more heavy lifting on the critical path.
options: You will get a personal assistant and an executive wardrobe allowance.
You are expected to work unpaid overtime doing the tasks of three vacant positions.
You need to hit the corporate gym and lift heavier weights.
Your workload will be reduced by 50% to maintain work-life balance.
exercises.why: 'Wear multiple hats' is hiring code for 'we understaffed this team by 60%.'

lessons.title: Executive Presence & Pivoting
lessons.description: Speaking with unearned authority and calling panicked roadmap collapses "pivots".

exercises.model: Agreeing with the highest paid person's opinion
exercises.snark: The corporate equivalent of synchronised nodding.
ideaLabels: deferring to the highest paid boss

exercises.model: Actually useful for once
exercises.snark: The elusive metric every PowerPoint deck swears it delivers.

exercises.model: The one thing we haven't outsourced yet
exercises.snark: What the company still knows how to do without hiring McKinsey.

exercises.model: Being rude under the guise of feedback
exercises.snark: Treating basic interpersonal tact as a barrier to velocity.

pairs: Agreeing with the highest paid person's opinion
The one thing we haven't outsourced yet
Being rude under the guise of feedback

exercises.email: The previous microservice architecture hit bandwidth limits. We need an agile pivot to demonstrate synergistic alignment with our core competencies.
options: The architecture worked perfectly according to plan.
The system collapsed and they are abandoning it while using buzzwords to save face.
The team is going on a synchronized gymnastics retreat.
Customers asked for fewer features.
exercises.why: 'Agile pivot' when infrastructure crashes is euphemistic surrender wrapped in consultants' jargon.

boss.title: The Performance Review Reframe
boss.prompt: Explain why the entire quarterly launch was missed without admitting fault. Reframe the disaster as strategic visionary flexibility and proactive team evolution.
boss.hint: Try using phrases like: 'agile pivot', 'opportunity for growth', 'growth mindset', 'comfortable with ambiguity', 'wear multiple hats', or 'critical path'.

title: Unit 4: LinkedIn Announcements
description: Dissect the humblebrag, visionary catalysts, and the existential question: Agree?

lessons.title: The Humblebrag Awakening
lessons.description: How getting laid off transforms into a transcendent spiritual milestone.

exercises.model: Arrogant and bragging
exercises.snark: The mandatory opening ritual for announcing a standard mid-level job hop.

exercises.text: Excited to share my next chapter
exercises.model: I got hired somewhere else for slightly more money
exercises.snark: Dramatizing a corporate transfer as a hero's epic literary voyage.

exercises.model: Please leave comments to boost my engagement algorithm
exercises.snark: Ending an irrelevant anecdote with a single-word engagement trap.

exercises.model: I was laid off or quit in rage
exercises.snark: The green banner that translates to 'available for recruiters immediately.'

pairs: Excited to share my next chapter
I got hired somewhere else for slightly more money
Please leave comments to boost my engagement algorithm
I was laid off or quit in rage

exercises.email: Humbled and thrilled to announce our game-changing milestone! We disrupted the paradigm and supercharged growth to unlock unprecedented synergies. Agree?
options: The company cured a disease or accomplished something historic.
They changed a button color from blue to indigo and need social media engagement.
Preston is feeling humble and quiet about the accomplishment.
The company is going bankrupt tomorrow.
exercises.why: 'Humbled and thrilled' combined with 'Agree?' is classic LinkedIn engagement bait for trivial updates.

lessons.title: Visionaries & Ecosystem Plays
lessons.description: Consultants with Canva accounts preaching holistic synergy optimization.

exercises.model: Sell the exact same software with a subscription fee
exercises.snark: Rebranding ordinary business concepts with revolutionary fervor.
ideaLabels: selling the same thing with a subscription

exercises.model: We shipped a minor patch
exercises.snark: Celebrating a dropdown menu redesign as humanity's moon landing.

exercises.model: Here is how my huge mistake actually proved I am a genius
exercises.snark: The humblebrag post dissecting an obvious failure into 7 bullet points.
ideaLabels: reframing a blunder into a genius lesson

exercises.model: Spend venture capital on ads recklessly
exercises.snark: Burning runway at maximum velocity to generate impressive top-line charts.

pairs: Sell the exact same software with a subscription fee
Here is how my huge mistake actually proved I am a genius
Spend venture capital on ads recklessly

exercises.subject: Strategic Transformation & Next Chapter
exercises.email: As part of our commitment to future-proof the business and optimize our north star metric, we are unlocking synergies by empowering team members to explore new external horizons.
options: Everyone is receiving an annual bonus and stock options.
The company is laying off a large percentage of the workforce today.
The company is launching an astronomy research telescope.
Employees are being sent to Hawaii on a corporate retreat.
exercises.why: 'Unlocking synergies' and 'exploring new external horizons' are the ultimate corporate euphemisms for layoffs.

lessons.title: Agree? Paradigm Disruption
lessons.description: Ending completely absurd anecdotes with single-word algorithmic engagement traps.

exercises.model: Things changed slightly
exercises.snark: Elevating mundane market fluctuations to epochal historical events.

exercises.model: The single number we manipulate to get funded
exercises.snark: A chosen metric designed to always go up and to the right.

exercises.model: Looking at more than two rows of data
exercises.snark: Taking 20 minutes to read the spreadsheet you should have read last week.

exercises.model: Ship buggy code and let support handle the fallout
exercises.snark: Glorifying carelessness until a security audit happens.

pairs: The single number we manipulate to get funded
Looking at more than two rows of data
Ship buggy code and let support handle the fallout

exercises.subject: Disrupting the Ecosystem from Zero to One
exercises.email: I had coffee with a 10x engineer this morning. Here are 5 lessons from failure on why having a seat at the table will supercharge your holistic flywheel. Agree?
options: Harrison has valuable proprietary business secrets to share.
Harrison is reciting hollow Silicon Valley clichés to harvest likes from strangers.
Harrison bought a literal table and flywheel for his garage.
Harrison is offering free engineering consulting.
exercises.why: A post listing '5 lessons from failure' ending with 'Agree?' is pure algorithm optimization with zero substance.

boss.title: The LinkedIn Phoenix
boss.prompt: You were abruptly let go this morning. Write a viral LinkedIn post reframing this severance event as an inspirational, transcendent milestone. Solicit engagement at the end!
boss.hint: Try using phrases like: 'humbled and thrilled', 'next chapter', 'agree?', 'open to new opportunities', 'paradigm shift', or 'game-changing milestone'.
